input.summary:
Boarding west bunk room (box x50..53 z10..12 y8..11): four brown_bed bunks via bed_set along the north wall (heads at z10 against the wall, feet z11), the z12 lane kept clear from the door, and one lantern hung on an iron_chain at (51,10..11,12) over the door line.
On a stand-in shell (floor, walls, ceiling, door added to a copy) the room has 0 dark floor cells (min light 10, 0 dim) and the fit check is OK; the walk is unverified because the entrance is far outside this part.
make.sh produced a whole build.nbt with my part placed (10 cells, no REFUSED, no OFF-PALETTE). No chests, carpets or flower pots: the four beds fill the room and the palette has no chest or pot.

waste.what: Checked walkability, light and fit by writing a stand-in shell (floor at y7, walls, ceiling at y12, door opening) into a copy of build.nbt with a throwaway script, because shell B and the roof are still stubs and the room tool otherwise reports 'no way in' and floating beds.
waste.cost: about 3 tool calls and one test script; the room tool's verdict on the real build stays NEEDS WORK until the shell lands
waste.tool: a `mcd room --assume-shell` (or a shell-stub flag) that fills a missing floor, perimeter walls and ceiling from rooms.json before judging, so an interior part can be checked before its neighbours are built

waste.what: Guessed the bed head/foot cells and the lane by hand from the 4x3 room and the plan, with no layout solver for a tight room of beds and a walk lane.
waste.cost: about 4 reasoning passes on the layout; the lane arithmetic (8 bed cells + 4 lane cells = the whole room) was done by hand
waste.tool: `layers()` with a bed legend, or a `mcd furnish --room` that tries bed/chest/lane arrangements against the walk and light checks and reports the best

waste.what: The plan tool drew the walls around the room as 'D' doorways and the room tool printed floor y=9 when the shell was missing, so I could not trust either until I had worked out the cause myself.
waste.cost: 2 extra room/plan runs to understand the output
waste.tool: `mcd plan` should mark a missing floor or wall as '?' rather than 'D', and print the floor level it assumed

companions.task: Confirm the chain-hung lantern at (51,10..11,12) once the roof part sets the y 12 ceiling, and move it if the ceiling is missing or the lantern floats.
Build the real floor at y7, the north and west walls, the z13 door and the landing so the room tool's walk reaches the lane from the door and the bunk feet.
Find storage (a chest or barrel dresser) for a 4x3 bunk room of four beds, since the lane takes the whole front row; I could only place the beds and the light.

left: No chest or storage: the four beds fill the north half and the z12 lane takes the front row, so there is no free cell for a barrel or chest dresser. The palette has no chest, carpet or flower pot, so none were placed.

The walk verdict on the real build is not yet OK: shell B (floor, walls, door, landing) and the roof part are still stubs, so the room tool reports 'no way in' and floating beds. On a stand-in shell the fit was OK and the light min was 10 with 0 dark cells; the walk was not confirmed end to end.
The hanging lantern relies on a y 12 ceiling above the chain at (51,11,12); if the roof part leaves y 12 open, the lantern floats and needs another support.
The visual check was inconclusive: the stand-in ceiling hid the room from above and the beds did not read in the render, so I did not confirm the look from inside.
elements.md's line for the boarding bunk rooms (west 4 beds and east 3 beds) is left unticked, since this part covers only the west room.
